rationale: Both responses give accurate summaries: first/last layers and the LM head are sensitive, down and output projections more so, sensitivity is driven by outliers and salient channels, and a small fraction of layers carries most of the loss. Both propose sensible label-free allocation pipelines with per-layer KL or perplexity, held-out validation and explicit assumptions. A has a clever negative-control validation (swap the 8- and 4-bit assignments) and a sequential knee check. B is somewhat more rigorous and complete. It grounds sensitivity in Fisher or Hessian curvature (HAWQ-style), computed self-supervised on unlabelled text, alongside activation and weight-outlier statistics, then confirms with end-to-end perturbation. It derives the number of 8-bit layers from a target average bit-width. Its validation compares against an all-4-bit baseline and sweeps the 8-bit fraction to find the knee, with concrete top-1 agreement and failure thresholds. Its assumption table states why each assumption matters. A's justification of additive error via GPTQ is weak, and some of its numeric thresholds are loosely stated. B also covers more of the literature (HAWQ, SpQR, QuIP#). Overall B is the stronger design.
